newsitem.title: DUBAI: Iran, Saudi to expand aviation links.
newsitem.headline: Iran, Saudi to expand aviation links.

text.p: Iran and Saudi Arabia on Sunday signed an agreement to expand aviation cooperation and launch the first direct flights between the two countries since the 1979 Islamic revolution in Iran.
Iran's official news agency IRNA said two flights a week would be launched soon between Tehran and the Saudi commercial capital Jeddah on the Red Sea. It gave no further details.
Iran Air is only allowed to directly fly to Jeddah to take Iranian Moslem pilgrims during the annual haj. Saudi Arabian Airlines Corp does not fly to Tehran.

The memorandum of understanding was signed in the western Saudi city of Medina by Abdel-Rahman al-Khalaf, head of the kingdom's civil aviation authority, and his Iranian counterpart, Ali Shahcheraghi.

Iran's ties with Saudi Arabia, the most influential Gulf country and custodian of Islam's two holiest shrines, have been tense since Iran's revolution in 1979. Tehran has recently been trying to improve ties with Saudi Arabia and other Gulf allies.
